Applications are submitted electronically.Â All application materials should be submitted to the College of Graduate Studies.
A $45 non-refundable application fee is required for U.S Citizens or U.S. permanent
resident card holders.Â
A $75 non-refundable application fee is required for international students.
Applications are considered for Fall Semester entrance only. Priority application deadline is December 15th. International applicants should also
have completed their current program by May 1. The number of available Ph.D. and M.S.
positions varies each year and depends upon faculty research funding. Only funded
faculty can accept students into their labs.Â Â
For more information visit the graduate admission process webpage.Â
Degree Requirements
Applicants must hold an earned 4 year baccalaureate degree (or equivalent) from an
accredited college or university, and have a minimum overall GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.
Typically, applicants will have an undergraduate major in Biology or a related discipline
such as Biochemistry or Biophysics.Â Students with other majors such as Chemistry or
Physics are encouraged to apply, but their coursework should include several semesters
in biology.Â
A Masterâs degree is not required to apply to a PhD program.Â
Laboratory research is highly recommended for all applicants.Â
GRE Requirement
GRE scores are not required for admission.Â
Proof of English Language ProficientÂ
International applicants will need to submit English Proficiency Scores (See Below).
The University of Toledo institution code is 1845. Scores should be no more than 2
years old.
TOEFL- Submit through ETS
IELTS- Submit through IELTS
PTE- Submit through Pearson PTE
Duolingo 110- Submit through Doulingo
All international applicants must provide proof of English language proficiency. The
following exceptions apply:
Proof of citizenship from one of these english text-exempt countries.
Successful completion of a U.S. Bachelor's or Master's degree.
Successful completion of at least 24 credit hours of academic study at a U.S. college
or university.Â
Any request for a waiver of the English language proficiency requirement must be submitted
to the Graduate Admissions Office with supporting documentation and will be reviewed
for approval.Â
Questions regarding the English language proficiency: Contact College of Graduate
Studies 419.530.4723 or graduateonlineapplication@utoledo.edu
Â
Transcripts
University of Toledo students do not need to send their current University of Toledo
transcripts. YouÂ mustÂ list the University of Toledo in the academic history section of your application
for admission.
Contact all previous higher education institutions you attended and have them send
your official transcripts to the University of Toledo following the guidelines below.Â
We cannot process your application until we receive your transcripts. â¯Â
A transcript is only considered official if it is sent electronically from the issuing
institution directly to the University of Toledo, or (if hard copy) it is in the original
sealed envelope with a registrarâs stamp intact.
Electronic transcripts are preferred.Â When ordering electronic copies from your previous
institution, please choose University of Toledo or University of Toledo Graduate Admissions.Â
Transcripts should indicate degree earned, date of conferral, and a key to the grading
system used.
Transcripts and diplomas should be submitted in their original language.
International Transcripts
Evaluations of foreign educational credentials areÂ required.Â
All credential evaluations must be from one of our four approved partners:
Educational Credential Evaluators (ECE), International Education Evaluations (IEE),
SpanTran, or World Education Services (WES).
Ordering Evaluations Using ECE
Please visit theÂ ECE websiteÂ and select theÂ Course by Course Report. Review the ECE officialÂ documentation requirementsÂ carefully, as they vary by country.
Ordering Evaluations Using IEE
IEE has 3-day guaranteed standard processing time and offers a reduced fee of $145
exclusively for UToledo applicants.Â To receive the discounted rate, please visit
theÂ IEE websiteÂ and order theÂ Education Course Report.
Ordering Evaluations Using SpanTran
SpanTran offers a 20% discount and 5 business day standard turnaround exclusively
for UToledo applicants. To receive the discounted rate, please visit theÂ SpanTran websiteÂ for additional details.Â
Ordering Evaluations Using WES
Please visitÂ WESÂ and order theÂ Course-by-Course International Credential Advantage Package (ICAP).
When ordering your evaluation you must designate the University of Toledo Graduate
Admissions as the recipient of all credential evaluations. The electronic evaluation
report will be delivered directly to UToledo.
Please note:Â If you have only one copy of a foreign transcript or diploma, please
visit the Graduate Admissions Office with your documents upon arrival to campus.
For more information, visit the How to Apply webpage.
Letters of Recommendation
Three letters of recommendation are required. The online application process will
provide you with the opportunity to send electronic requests to your recommenders.
Statement of Purpose
Applicants are required to provide a statement of purpose that highlights academic
and research training prior to application. Applicants should discuss future career
goals and why they are interested in UToledo.
Resume/CV
Applicants are required to submit a resume/curriculum vitae.

The objective of the University of Toledo is to increase opportunities for persons
with disabilities, while maintaining the expectation that all students achieve the
goals of our programs. The technical standards for admission establish the expectations
and abilities considered essential for students admitted to the Ph.D./M.S. in Biomedical
Science program in order to achieve the level of competency required for graduation.Â
All students must have at the time of admission, and demonstrate throughout their
course of study, a fundamental respect for truth and a commitment to honest reporting
of experimental results.
In addition, all students admitted to the Ph.D./M.S. in Biomedical Science program
are expected to be able to demonstrate the abilities below:
must have the mental capacity to assimilate, within a reasonable time, a large amount
of scientific information in the area of biomedical sciences
must have the ability to communicate effectively with all persons involved in graduate
training; where such training involves interacting with additional persons (e.g.,
patients or volunteers for experiments), an effective level of communication skill
is similarly required
must be able to master concepts, show evidence of a reasonable level of deductive
reasoning, and be able to acquire the essential skills needed for presentation of
research data
must possess sufficient postural control, neuromuscular control and eye-to-hand control
to independently use standard laboratory/medical/surgical instruments
must have the ability to independently perform, at a reasonable level, all laboratory
or other manipulations required for research leading to the Ph.D. or M.S. in Biomedical
Sciences degree
Candidates are urged to ask questions about the programâs technical standards for
clarification and to determine whether they can meet the requirements.Â Questions
may be directed to the program director.Â Revealing a disability is voluntary; however,
such disclosure is necessary before any accommodations may be considered in the learning
environment or in the programâs procedures.Â
Information about disabilities is handled in a confidential manner. Reasonable accommodations
will be made to qualified applicants with a disability in such circumstances and on
such terms as required by the Americans with Disabilities Act.Â Reasonable accommodations
require program and institutional approval.Â Requests for accommodations must be submitted
in writing, allowing sufficient time prior to matriculation for action on these requests,
pursuant to Policy 01-061 Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability, Americans
with Disabilities Act Compliance.
College of Graduate Studies (COGS)
For specific information about the status of your application, as well as other inquiries
about general application requirements, you may contact COGS atÂ (419) 530-4723Â orÂ graduateonlineapplication@utoledo.edu.
Office of Registrar
Â The Office of the Registrar provides services related to studentsâ academic records.
The office can help with registration, transcripts, and graduation. Health Science
Campus Registrar office is located on the 1st floor of the Mulford Library. Feel free to email the Office of the Registrar at registrar@utoledo.edu
Office of International Students & Scholar Services (OISSS)Â
TheÂ Office of International Student and Scholar Services (OISSS)Â provides assistance and services to international students at The University
of Toledo, helping students transition to life at UToledo and in the United States.
Serves as a resource for orientation, visa requirements, on-campus and off-campus
housing, banking, and international student health insurance.
Â
Ph.D. students (domestic and international) in good standing are eligible to receive
a full tuition scholarship, stipend that is at the National Institutes of Health/National
Research Service award level ($28,000 per year), and health insurance. Ph.D. students
are not required to be teaching assistants to receive the tuition scholarship and
stipend, although teaching experiences are available to interested students.
Â
Frequently Asked Questions
Do I need to find a mentor before I apply or enter the program?
Students accepted into our program do not need to find a mentor before they enter.
All students undergo laboratory rotations during their first year and then make a
mutual decision with a mentor for their dissertation research.
Do students receiving funding?
All PhD students receive a living stipend of $28,000 per year, tuition waiver, and
health insurance.Â
The Biomedical Science Program research tracks are no longer able to offer any funding
support for MS applicants.
Â
Is teaching a requirement of the program/stipend?
No, students are not required to complete teaching assistantships.Â
Do you offer application fee waivers?
We are unable to offer application fee waivers.Â
Â
How many students are accepted each year?
The number of students accepted various from year to year. We encourage applicants
to apply early before the priority deadline of December 15th for best consideration.Â
